requestedItems.quote: Include Basil and Mint, practical setup steps, watering and harvesting advice
requestedItems.coverageQuote:
Basil
Practical Setup Steps
- Container: Use a pot with drainage holes, at least 12 inches deep.
- Soil: Well-drained soil with rich organic matter.
- Location: Place in a sunny spot with 6-8 hours of sunlight.
Watering and Harvesting Advice
- Watering: Water deeply when the top inch of soil is dry.
- Harvesting: Pinch off leaves regularly to encourage growth and prevent
flowering.

requestedItems.quote: Include Basil and Mint, practical setup steps, watering and harvesting advice
requestedItems.coverageQuote:
Mint
Practical Setup Steps
- Container: Use a wide container, as mint spreads aggressively.
- Soil: Loamy soil, slightly acidic to neutral pH.
- Location: Can tolerate some shade, but prefers partial sun.
Watering and Harvesting Advice
- Watering: Keep soil consistently moist, but not waterlogged.
- Harvesting: Harvest leaves as needed, trim back regularly to maintain
shape.

independentInspection.text: Balcony Herb Plan Introduction Growing herbs on your balcony can be a rewarding and practical way to enhance your culinary dishes and enjoy gardening in limited space. This guide provides practical steps for setting up a small balcony herb garden, focusing on Basil and Mint. Basil Practical Setup Steps - Container: Use a pot with drainage holes, at least 12 inches deep. - Soil: Well-drained soil with rich organic matter. - Location: Place in a sunny spot with 6-8 hours of sunlight. Watering and Harvesting Advice - Watering: Water deeply when the top inch of soil is dry. - Harvesting: Pinch off leaves regularly to encourage growth and prevent flowering. Mint Practical Setup Steps - Container: Use a wide container, as mint spreads aggressively. - Soil: Loamy soil, slightly acidic to neutral pH. - Location: Can tolerate some shade, but prefers partial sun. Watering and Harvesting Advice - Watering: Keep soil consistently moist, but not waterlogged. - Harvesting: Harvest leaves as needed, trim back regularly to maintain shape. Safety Note Mint can become invasive. Keep it contained by planting in a separate pot or use a root barrier if planted directly in a larger container. Conclusion By following these steps, you can successfully grow and maintain Basil and Mint on your balcony. Enjoy fresh herbs ready for your recipes anytime!
